newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: German arrested in Colombia said on government mission.
newsitem.headline: German arrested in Colombia said on government mission.

text.p: A German arrested for trying to smuggle a rebel kidnap victim out of Colombia had the backing of his government and of a former Siemens executive, a diplomat and employee for the German company said on Tuesday.

Helmut Luecker, a German consul, told RCN radio network the man, whose real name is thought to be Werner Mauss, and his female companion were involved in a "humanitarian mission ... with the approval of the German government."

He did not elaborate and the German Embassy in Bogota has maintained a media blackout since the arrests. But a Western diplomat said "it would seem to be stretching the imagination to think Mauss was working without the knowledge" of the German diplomatic mission in Colombia.
Mauss was arrested along with 36-year-old Silvia Schroder early on Sunday as they tried to bundle Brigitte Schoene, also a German, aboard a plane in Rionegro airport near Medellin.
Colombia's National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrilla group had kidnapped Schoene, the wife of a former BASF Chemicals executive, on Aug. 15 and had been demanding as much as $6 million ransom.

Barbara Hinzer, an official of Siemens-Colombia, said she hired the charter plane that was to be used by Mauss but she had been misled about its purpose. She said she hired the plane as a personal favour for Ariel Sharef, the former head of Siemens-Colombia, who left the company and Colombia about three months ago.

"He called me last week. It was, as far as I knew, to fly a group of German conference delegates from Medellin to Cartagena. It was a private agreement and had nothing to do with Siemens-Colombia," Hinzer said.

Mauss, 56, has a reputation as a loose cannon, often working to secure the release of hostages held by guerrilla armies, according to German media reports. Western diplomatic sources described Mauss as a "maverick."

Adding to the mystery surrounding the German agent, Colombian Interior Minister Horacio Serpa said on Tuesday that he met Mauss during a visit to Germany in July when he travelled there to discuss the possibility of Germany hosting future peace talks with Colombia's leftist rebels.

Serpa said Mauss appeared to be very well-connected in government circles in Germany but he was unable to comment on his alleged ties to the ELN. Colombian police and local government officials maintain that Mauss is a shadowy member of the ELN and one of its chief financiers abroad.
